**Test image key features:**
- Large, dark brown/black irregular necrotic lesion covering the upper-center portion of the leaf
- Somewhat angular/irregular edges that appear vein-bounded
- Remaining leaf tissue is green
- Background shows some yellowing on other plants
- Single leaf held by hand close-up

**Assessment of candidates:**
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular water-soaked spots turning brown with reddish-brown centers + yellowish-green halos; can coalesce into large irregular lesions. The angular nature of the lesion in the test image is consistent with vein-bounded bacterial spread. This fits best.
- **Phyllosticta**: Gray/tan lesions with dark margins — the test image lesion is too dark brown/black
- **Cercospora**: Diffuse purple/bronze discoloration — the test image has a discrete dark lesion rather than diffuse coloring
- **SDS**: Interveinal chlorosis with scattered brown spots — different pattern
- **Anthracnose**: Primarily stem/pod focused
- **Septoria brown spot**: Multiple small angular red-brown spots, not one large lesion

The large irregular dark brown lesion with angular edges (bounded by veins) is most consistent with **coalesced Bacterial_Blight** lesions — the description explicitly states "lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions" with "dark reddish-brown centers."
